speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are experiencing fatigue, difficulty concentrating, and abnormal blood findings; to understand the root cause, have you noticed any unexplained weight loss or fever recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 53-year-old male. The patient has a 3-week history of fatigue, difficulty to concentrate, and dyspnea on exertion. He also experiences dizziness and digital pain that improves with cold. He has a long history of smoking.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. The combination of fatigue, dizziness, and digital pain that improves with cold strongly suggests Raynaud's phenomenon, but the abnormal blood findings require clarification. Have you noticed any swelling in your hands or feet, or any skin color changes beyond the digits?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fatigue and difficulty to concentrate. I also have Dyspnea on exertion, Dizziness, Digital pain that improves with cold.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Systemic Sclerosis (Scleroderma) with secondary Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.

The clinical picture of Raynaud's phenomenon, exertional dyspnea, dizziness, and fatigue in a 53-year-old male with a smoking history strongly suggests early systemic sclerosis complicated by pulmonary hypertension. The abnormal blood findings likely reflect anemia or renal involvement. Please confirm if you have a history of skin thickening on your fingers or face, and request a Pulmonary Function Test with DLCO and an Echocardiogram to assess right heart strain and gas exchange.
